speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the rationale behind barring women above 45 years old from receiving in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) treatments in Singapore; (b) what is the rationale behind limiting the number of IVF fresh cycles for women above 40 years old; and (c) whether the Ministry is planning to review these restrictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The success rates of Assisted Reproduction (AR) procedures decrease and the likelihood of medical complications and adverse pregnancy outcomes increases with maternal age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It is, therefore, important that patients are well informed of the risks and outcomes of such procedures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, the Ministry of Health (MOH) considers appeals on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is because there are increased clinical risks with multiple cycles of ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These risks include ovarian hyper-stimulation syndrome, bleeding and infection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We recognise that recent advancements in AR technology have improved the safety of AR procedures in general.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Government reviews these limits regularly and will take into account such technological advancements and other medical and social considerations, including the risk of chronic diseases, pregnancy or delivery complications, and continued low success rates of pregnancy and live births for women of higher maternal age.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the concerns and risks that she mentioned, but these are concerns and risks that parents should consider and decide whether they want to have a child, and not something that the Government should decide.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, whether MOH will review this policy of restricting the number of IVF cycles after age 40 and restricting IVF completely after 45; and two, how long will such a review take?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In Singapore, the current AR age limit of 45 is set based on empirical evidence that shows that the chances of conception are very low at older ages.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, there are also increased medical risks and complications as well as adverse pregnancy outcomes for women of older ages.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said in my reply, this is really set to protect the patients' interests.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Nonetheless, MOH does consider appeals on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the treatment cycle limit of five fresh cycles for women above the age of 40, again, this is due to concerns of increased clinical risks with older ages, with multiple cycles of ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But what all this is driving is that these parents who want to have kids are just going to Johor to do the IVF cycles, and that places a lot of undue stress on them to travel to another country to do something that they want to do which our Government is prohibiting them to do.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: My response will be that, as I have said, even as there are advancements made in AR technology and it is safer and lower risk now to women for the AR procedure, we need to continue to highlight to couples who want children that notwithstanding the advancement in AR technology, the chances of conception, of pregnancy, at older ages have not increased, remain low.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The medical risk and adverse pregnancy outcomes also remain.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That has to be highlighted, so that they do not have false high expectations of success for such AR procedures at older ages.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Just a quick clarification for the Senior Minister of State.
